messages:
emma: quick thought — canary switchover edge cases i ran into when sessions stick to old variant after fallback. steps: if we route back to stable, user sees truncated convo or duplicated tokens. need plan.

raj: hmm yep. is this mostly after model variant mismatch or kv-cache eviction?

emma: variant + different kv layout. when we reroute mid-session the new variant expects different KV keys. result: gibberish or runtime errors in generation.

miguel: SRE note: we saw elevated 500s and p50 spikes on one canary last week, likely cache-mismatch.

claire: product concern: if user gets partial reply or 'incoherent' text that's a bad UX. we need a safe fallback that preserves session fidelity.

raj: two options: (1) session affinity pinned to variant until refill completes, or (2) encode session compatibility version and do transform/rehydration on switchover.

emma: we prototyped a rehydration shim: on switchover, we replay last N tokens to rebuild KV on new variant. works but adds ~30-80ms per session on first request.

miguel: 30-80ms may be acceptable if only first request post-switchover. still need to track cost.

claire: metrics to drive: user-visible error rate, incoherence evals, p99 latency, cost delta. want explicit thresholds for auto-fallback.

raj: propose policy: ramp traffic -> observe 5m window signals (error_rate>1% OR p99 increase >200ms) -> hold and attempt rehydrate path -> if rehydrate fails or cost delta > 1.5x then rollback. also allow manual override.

deploy-bot: deploy event: canary-variant/v2 started at 3712345678

emma: edge case: frequent micro-switchoffs cause repeated rehydration leading to noise. need cooldown per session: once rehydrated, pin for T minutes (e.g., 15m).

miguel: also consider probe requests to warm KV proactively during rollout: background warmup traffic to some session shadows.

raj: agree. Pseudoconfig:
```
rollout:
  ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 30m
  signals:
    error_rate: 1%
    p99_delta_ms: 200
  on_signal:
    attempt_rehydrate: true
    session_cooldown_min: 15
```

claire: question: who owns the rehydration shim? runtime team or model onboarding? we need clear interface.

emma: runtime should expose rehydrate API: /rehydrate?session_id=... returns success/failure and cost estimate. onboarding provides transformer compatibility hints.

miguel: ops-bot suggestion: log events with tag rollout_id + session_id + outcome to make postmortems easier.

ops-bot: note: creating alert rule channel=incidents if rollout_failure_count > 3 in 10m

raj: final: I'll write a short RFC for the runtime rehydrate API + rollout policy DSL. want implementation owners: runtime (raj/emma), onboarding (claire), sres (miguel).

emma: thanks — i'll start a branch and ping for review. :thumbsup:
